baseline_and_finding.original_three_gap_baseline: At WI056 closeout / WI059 activation, python -m repopact.cli validate reported exactly three diagnostics: unsupported.semantic-surface for governance/adopters.json ('adopter fleet validation'), unsupported.semantic-surface for research/metadata.json ('research metadata validation'), and work.readme-checkbox-missing for completed WI036's AC-7 criterion.
baseline_and_finding.cvp_017_fixture_amplification: Before WI059 semantic work began, a full-baseline attempt discovered that several Python test fixtures recursively copied the entire developer checkout with an incomplete ignore list that did not exclude rust/target, causing multi-gigabyte-per-run storage amplification unrelated to WI059 semantics. Fixed by centralizing fixture materialization in repopact/dev_fixtures.py (git-aware file selection, disabled Git auto-maintenance in disposable repos, guaranteed cleanup, anti-recursion guard). See work-item CVP-017 and fixture-storage-finding.md.
baseline_and_finding.sol_review_containment_correction: A subsequent architecture review found that RecordIndex::build_with_topology read metadata-directed adopter-overlay and research-reference paths into source_paths/text_files/adopter_overlay_bytes before any containment check could reject an escaping reference (e.g. '../outside.txt' or an absolute path outside the repository), so external content could be ingested into the immutable snapshot even though validation would eventually reject it. Fixed with one reusable repopact_repository::resolve_within_root(root, relative) choke point (canonicalize-based, symlink-aware, no content read to decide) used by both the snapshot builder and the adopter/research validators, plus an equivalent _resolve_local()/_require_local() containment check added to the explicit Python comparator (validate_research.py) so Rust and Python do not drift on this boundary. See commits 8606f31 (Rust) and ba339f9 (Python).
